agent_messages.text: I’ll read the pinned goal, full design, audits and latest artifacts, then choose a research step that preserves the full conjecture’s scope. I’ll checkpoint results under unique paths and distinguish proofs from experiments.

The latest work leaves an auxiliary convolution inequality open on the upper interval; even closing it would leave other regions and directions of the full conjecture unresolved. I’ll investigate that inequality while keeping those obligations explicit. The environment denies access to `.scratch`, so I’ll use unique `research/` and `evidence/` paths.

A broader shortcut failed: log-concavity of the weight sequence alone does not imply the needed convolution-ratio inequality. The exact-arithmetic counterexample is auxiliary, not a Markov counterexample. I’ll check which features of the actual weights \(1,4,8,12,\ldots\) matter.

I found a small exact obstruction to the general-weight shortcut: weights \([1,3,9,1]\) give gap \(-28620\), despite being log-concave. For the actual weights, I’m formalizing an explicit evaluation of the four-row determinants used in the proposed Schur approach. This would settle their signs and vanishing, but the expansion and its coefficient-sign proof would still be open.

Lean has verified the arbitrary-weight obstruction, including zero-extended `CrossLC`. I also derived a positive formula for the next-to-final step of the actual kernel’s ratio inequality. The remaining work there is to attach that formula to the polynomial coefficients and check the resulting theorem.

Lean has verified the four-row determinant formulas: for a partition \((a,b,c,d)\), the determinant vanishes exactly when \(c\ge3\), and is strictly positive otherwise. This settles the determinant-sign question from the inherited experiment. I’m now checking a falling-factorial reformulation of the remaining upper interval to make its unresolved inequality more explicit.

The exact upper-interval reformulation and the deficiency-three certificate now compile. This leaves an explicit residual for \(4\le h\le j\); it remains open. A separate source scan checked 25,161 coefficients, retaining 11,363 zeros, and 208,455 polygon-valid triples across all three directions without a failure. Those scan results are finite evidence only.

The remaining inequality now has an exact integer form in Lean: `ClearedCoreMBEC` is equivalent to the inherited upper-interval condition. The first eight new modules passed joint kernel replay, and their 41 theorem closures use only permitted axioms. The nine-module replay, including the integer reformulation, is running.

All ten new mathematical modules passed joint kernel replay, and all 56 audited theorem closures use only permitted axioms. The polynomial certificate now has a proved evaluation and source-transport bridge; its universal coefficient positivity remains open. Larger fixed-\(h\) experiments also found positive coefficients, without resolving that obligation. I’m finishing the preservation checks and handoff report.

decls={m:re.findall(r'^theorem\s+(\w+)',(R/'research'/f'{m}.lean').read_text(),re.M) for m in mods}
src='\n'.join('import '+m for m in mods)+'\n'
for ns in decls.values():
 for n in ns:src+='#print axioms MathGKM.Markov.'+n+'\n'

(R/'research'/f'{name}.lean').write_text(src)
